hypotheses.justification: The statement `D.V k = D.O k` only uses `V`, `O`, `ιι`, `Ω` and `π`. These are defined in the `Setup` section and need only `[CommRing A]`, so the Noetherian hypothesis does not appear in the statement. In the proof it enters only through `isNoetherian_X`, which uses `LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian` together with `QuasiCompact f`. That gives a Noetherian `X`, which feeds `noetherianSpace_Uo` and then `quasiCompact_ψ := inferInstance`. `QuasiCompact D.ψ` is what the chain needs: `IsDominant ψ'` and `IsOpenImmersion ψ'` (Mathlib instances `[QuasiCompact f] : IsDominant f.toImage` and `[IsImmersion f] [QuasiCompact f] : IsOpenImmersion f.toImage`), plus the support of the scheme-theoretic image in `irreducibleSpace_X'`. `QuasiCompact ψ` can be obtained without Noetherian hypotheses. First, `ψ ≫ pullback.fst f D.prπ = D.Uo.ι` (`ψ_fst`). Second, `pullback.fst f D.prπ` is the base change of the proper, hence separated, `prπ`, so it is quasi-separated. So `QuasiCompact.of_comp` (Mathlib, Morphisms/QuasiSeparated.lean) applies once `Uo.ι` is quasi-compact. That holds because each `U k` is affine: `c k` is a closed immersion into an affine `Spec`, and `isAffine_of_isAffineHom` applies. Also `X` is separated, hence quasi-separated, over the affine `Spec A` because `[IsSeparated f]`. So the finite intersection `Uo` is quasi-compact, and an open immersion of a quasi-compact open into a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-compact. The other ingredients do not use Noetherianity: reducedness and irreducibility of `X'` (from `IsIntegral X`), nonemptiness of `Uo`, `ak_eq_bk`, the closed immersion `ιΩ` and the properness of `ek` (from `IsSeparated f`). So the theorem stays true and provable without `[IsNoetherianRing A]`. The same reasoning lets `[LocallyOfFiniteType f]` and `[QuasiCompact f]` be dropped, each on its own or all together.

Not in the statement; the definitions `V`, `O`, `ιι`, `Ω` do not need it. In the proof it is used only in `isNoetherian_X`, to get `IsLocallyNoetherian X`. That in turn is used only to get `QuasiCompact D.ψ`, which feeds `IsDominant ψ'`, `IsOpenImmersion ψ'` and the irreducibility of `X'`. As explained for `[IsNoetherianRing A]`, `QuasiCompact ψ` follows otherwise. Use `QuasiCompact.of_comp` with `ψ ≫ pullback.fst f prπ = Uo.ι` (`ψ_fst`) and the fact that `pullback.fst f prπ` is quasi-separated, as a base change of the separated `prπ`. Here `Uo.ι` is quasi-compact: each `U k` is affine (closed immersion `c k` into an affine scheme, `isAffine_of_isAffineHom`), and `X` is quasi-separated because `f` is separated over an affine base. The rest of the argument does not involve finite type.

Not in the statement. In the proof it is used only in `isNoetherian_X`, via `QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f`, to make `X` compact and hence Noetherian. That only serves to get `QuasiCompact D.ψ` (and `CompactSpace XP`/`X'`, which `V_eq_O` does not need). `QuasiCompact ψ` comes from `QuasiCompact.of_comp` applied to `ψ ≫ pullback.fst f prπ = Uo.ι`. This works because `Uo` is a finite intersection of affine opens (each `U k` has a closed immersion `c k` into an affine scheme) in the quasi-separated scheme `X` (`f` is separated over affine `Spec A`), so `Uo.ι` is quasi-compact. Also `pullback.fst f prπ` is quasi-separated, as a base change of the proper `prπ`. Neither step uses quasi-compactness of `f`. The rest of the proof is unchanged: `IsSeparated f` gives properness of `ek`, and `IsIntegral X` gives connectedness of `O k` and nonemptiness of `V k`.
